AboutPage.metaDescription: Honest analytics for Hyperliquid traders. Learn what Steady does, who built it, and why it exists.
AboutPage.title: About Steady
AboutPage.intro: Steady is honest analytics for Hyperliquid traders. It helps you understand why you're losing money — and what to change.
AboutPage.why1: I'm a trader. I built Steady because every existing tool I tried felt like a coach paid to flatter me. They showed pretty charts, big numbers, motivational quotes. None of them told me the hard truth: I was losing because I revenge-trade after losses, scalp when I should swing, and use too much leverage on coins I don't understand.
AboutPage.why2: I wanted a tool that would tell me what's wrong, factually, with my own data. So I built it.
AboutPage.what1: Reconstructs every trade you've made on Hyperliquid using FIFO accounting
AboutPage.what2: Calculates real metrics: win rate by direction, RR, drawdown, hold time, funding cost
AboutPage.what3: Detects behavioral patterns: revenge trading, scalping bias, drawdown patterns
AboutPage.what4: Generates a verdict and one concrete action to take
AboutPage.whatNote: All from your wallet's public on-chain data. No login. No API key. Read-only.
AboutPage.who1: Just one person. Currently in early beta — the product evolves daily based on user feedback.
AboutPage.whoContact: You can reach me on Twitter — fastest way to get a response.
AboutPage.pricing1: Steady is free during beta. A Pro tier ($19/month) will launch with multi-wallet support, full historical data, exports, and alerts.
AboutPage.pricing2: The free version will always include enough to be useful.

FaqPage.metaDescription: Frequently asked questions about Steady — data safety, accuracy, supported platforms, and more.
FaqPage.title: Frequently Asked Questions

q1.a: Yes. Steady uses only public on-chain data from Hyperliquid. We never ask for API keys, private keys, or login credentials. Your wallet is identified only by its public address — the same data anyone can see on the blockchain.

q2.q: Why do I need to enter my wallet address?
q2.a: To analyze your trading history. Steady fetches your public fills from Hyperliquid and reconstructs your trades using FIFO accounting. We cache the result so future visits load faster.

q3.a: Yes. DM us on Twitter @usesteadytrade with your wallet address and we'll clear it from Steady's cache within 48 hours. Note: the underlying data will still exist on Hyperliquid's public blockchain — only our cache is deleted.

q4.a: We use FIFO (First In First Out) accounting to match opens and closes — the same method used by professional tools like Cointracking. PnL totals match Hyperliquid's reported figures to the cent.

q5.q: Why does a whale's PnL look so different from what I expected?
q5.a: Whales scale in and out of positions thousands of times. Older tools treated their entire holding period as one trade. Steady uses FIFO to split it into individual round-trips. The total PnL is identical, but metrics like win rate and RR become meaningful.

q6.q: What if a position was opened before my analysis window?
q6.a: Steady analyzes a fixed time window (default 30 days). If a position was opened before your selected window, the entry price used in calculations comes from the first visible fill, not the actual entry. This is a known limitation of windowed analysis.

q7.q: What's the difference between Steady and Hyperliquid's own analytics?
q7.a: Hyperliquid shows your PnL and basic stats. Steady tells you why you're winning or losing — behavioral patterns, time-based performance, RR, and a concrete action to take.

q8.a: Cached data refreshes on demand (click "Refresh") or automatically after 1 hour. New trades show up the next time you analyze your address.

q9.q: Why isn't my favorite metric here?
q9.a: Because we haven't built it yet. Tweet your request to @usesteadytrade — most reasonable feature requests ship within a week.

q10.a: Not yet. Hyperliquid first because its data is fully on-chain and free to query. Binance and Bybit support is on the roadmap but requires API keys, which is a different security model.

q11.q: Is Steady available in other languages?
q11.a: Currently English and French. More languages will be added based on user demand.

q12.q: Can I use Steady on mobile?
q12.a: Yes — the app is fully mobile-responsive. A native iOS/Android app is not planned in the short term.

revenge.title: Revenge trading is costing you
revenge.explanation: {pct}% of your trades are taken within {window} min of a loss. They cost you {amount} over this period.
revenge.action: Block yourself from trading 1 hour after any closed loss.

scalping.title: Quick trades aren't your edge
scalping.explanation: {pct}% of your trades close in under 30 min — they cost you {amount}. Your longer trades made {longAmount}.
scalping.action: Aim for holds above 2 hours. Set a minimum timer before entering.

scalpingNoLong.title: Quick trades aren't your edge
scalpingNoLong.explanation: {pct}% of your trades close in under 30 min — they cost you {amount}. You never hold a position over 4 hours.
scalpingNoLong.action: Try one swing trade this week. Set a 4-hour minimum before closing a position.

drawdown.title: Risk management needs attention
drawdown.explanation: Your max drawdown reached -{pct}%. Professional traders typically cap at -15–20%.
drawdown.action: Reduce position size by 30–50% on your next trades.

decliningWR.title: Recent performance slipping
decliningWR.explanation: Your win rate over the last {days} days is {recent}% — {diff} points below your overall average of {total}%.
decliningWR.action: Take a 24h break and review your last 5 losses before trading again.

longBias.title: Bias detected: longs work, shorts don't
longBias.explanation: Long win rate: {longWR}%. Short win rate: {shortWR}%. Your shorts cost you {amount}.
longBias.action: Consider trading longs only for 2 weeks and track if results improve.

funding.title: Funding fees are eating your gains
funding.explanation: You paid {amount} in funding fees — that's {pct}% of your absolute P&L.
funding.action: Time exits before funding events. Avoid holding through high-rate periods.

success.title: Solid performance
success.explanation: Profitable, low drawdown, consistent win rate. Your discipline is paying off.
success.action: Don't change a winning approach. Resist the urge to size up impulsively.

neutral.title: Mixed signals
neutral.explanation: No clear pattern dominates your data yet. More trades will give clearer insights.
neutral.action: Continue trading and check back in 2 weeks.

BuyHold.title: Buy & Hold vs Active Trading
BuyHold.footerNote: Buy & hold assumes entering at your first trade's avg entry price and holding through your last exit, same size.

SteadyScore.title: Steady Score
SteadyScore.notEnough: Not enough data — trade more to unlock your score.
SteadyScore.philosophy: Steady Score measures your discipline, not your P&L. A profitable but undisciplined trader can score lower than a slightly losing but disciplined one.
